title: Impact of Inclusion of Capital Income on Singapore's Gini Coefficient
what_it_is: Impact of Inclusion of Capital Income on Singapore's Gini Coefficient

sections.label: Gini coefficient and capital income
sections.summary: MP asks about Gini coefficient with capital income; Ministry says such data is not included due to measurement issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Finance (a) what is the Gini coefficient of Singapore for each year in the past 10 years when capital income is taken into account; (b) if such data is not available, whether inclusion of capital income is likely to increase or decrease Singapore's Gini coefficient; and (c) whether the Ministry will take into account capital income when reporting Singapore's Gini coefficient.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This data is available annually and enables the timely tracking of income inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Collecting income data from sources other than work is more challenging.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Such data are typically collected based on self-reporting by respondents and are more susceptible to measurement errors.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: This is why the Department of Statistics has thus far not included such data in its computation of the Gini coefficient.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Nevertheless, the Government will continue to explore ways to better measure and monitor income inequality.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Regardless of the measurement issues, our approach remains to keep our social support measures progressive and targeted at the lower- and middle-income households.

sections.label: OECD capital income and surveys
sections.summary: OECD countries include capital income; Singapore's household expenditure survey covers non-work income but not in Gini computation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also understand that, for example, all the other Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) countries do include capital income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do have surveys of income other than work in the household expenditure survey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It is not part of the Gini coefficient computation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, that income is covered in the household expenditure survey which is done once every five years.
